recipes.name: Garlic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 6 chicken leg quarters, split into drumsticks and thighs
6 large Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into chunks
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Place the butter into a roasting pan, and melt in the oven, about 3 to 5 minutes. When butter is melted, swirl to coat the bottom of the roasting pan, placing the chicken drumsticks and thighs, potatoes, and unpeeled garlic cloves into the pan. Sprinkle with salt and black pepper; turn the chicken, potatoes, and garlic to coat with butter.

Bake in the preheated oven until the chicken is no longer pink inside and the juices run clear, about 40 minutes, basting 3 times with pan drippings. Remove from oven and brush maple syrup over the chicken pieces, and spoon pan drippings over the potatoes.

Return to oven, and bake until the chicken and potatoes are tender and browned, about 20 more minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into a thick part of a thigh should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). To serve, squeeze the tender roasted garlic from the cloves, spread it over the chicken, and drizzle the savory pan juices over the chicken and potatoes.

raw_recipe.headline: Garlic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Chicken and potatoes bake in butter with 24 cloves of garlic and a little maple syrup at the end for sweetness. Don’t worry, the garlic cooks down to a mellow, soft texture that’s perfect to spread over the buttery chicken.

video.description: I've been making this recipe for so many years, I can't remember where I got it from. It's really quick to throw together. After fixing it several times, my husband 'discovered' that you were supposed to spread the garlic on the chicken.
video.name: How to Make Garlic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes

review.reviewBody: I used drums only, as that is what I had on hand. It was so simple to throw together. I actually forgot the final step of the syrup but we loved it as it was. We are garlic lovers so this was great. Oh, I didn't have fresh cloves so I used jarred minced garlic. We didn't get to spread the garlic over the chicken but it baked into the drums and then covered the potatoes!! YUMMY!!

This was delicious and so easy! Thanks for sharing. I'm going to add a little more detail. I had a 4 pack of chicken thighs I wanted to use, so that's what I used instead what it called for. I only had a small square brownie type pan, so I used that instead of a roasting pan. I used one whole garlic cluster, separated and peeled, about 14 cloves or so. I had to bake it 20 extra minutes to get the thermometer to 165. I don't think it needed all that garlic, not that it hurt it at all, but you really only got the garlic taste by smooshing the cloves onto the chicken at the end, and each piece used about 2 cloves. It turned out great and the potatoes were to die for! I didn't have to add any salt once to them on my plate (which is unusual for me) and they were so buttery! I will be adding this dish to my regular rotation.
Yummy. Love this recipe and it is so easy. Added carrots and used red potatoes and chicken thighs. You'll want leftovers.

This was pretty tasty- I followed the recipe pretty closely just added a few extra veggies and some herbs. It smoked up my house pretty bad, but I can live with that.
It's four stars only because it was kind of greasy- a little too greasy for my taste. Too much butter I think.

I’ve been making this for years and had completely forgotten about it until the other day. I’m making it for Sunday dinner too! The only things I changed is I use minced garlic and change the salt and pepper to just Lawry’s seasoning salt. I season the potatoes first, then create a well with the garlic and butter dredge the chicken and use the seasoning salt on both sides. I then place the chicken on top of the potatoes. I don’t baste the syrup either, I just drizzle it over the top of everything. Such a delicious dish! I think the potatoes are my favorite. Thank you for this awesome recipe!

This meal is easy to make and very satisfying to enjoy. I put everything in a large dutch oven after I had browned the chicken on the stovetop in the dutch oven. I filled the remaining space with small red potatoes, cut up bell peppers, sliced red onion, and a few sprigs of rosemary. The sauce this makes is slightly sweet and delicious. Next time I’m going to top with a few cashews when ready to serve.

Great starter recipe! I had chicken legs so I used those, and added other veggies - Brussels sprouts and carrots with baby red potatoes. Added garlic powder to the seasoning because more garlic is always good. I also roasted my garlic separately and let it cool while the dish was roasting. When the chicken was done, it was easy to squeeze out the garlic and spread on each leg. I will be making this again and again, perfect Sunday dinner.

We loved this recipe! Simple yet flavorful. It’s not a quick cooking meal though but I still like the very minimal preparation and ingredients. I replaced the Yukon with sweet potatoes. I always buy my garlic peeled already but I still crushed it on the chicken starting at 40 minutes. I used salt, pepper and garlic powder on the chicken. Basting is an important step. Don’t skip this. I covered only after 40 minutes to release more juices.

Made it last night, but in a deeper glass dish, not on a flat tray (it splatters so much all over the oven, I hate cleaning it up). 35 min covered with foil, 25 min uncovered. DELICIOUS! Husband agreed and asked when am I making it again.

This recipe is amazing! Seriously, finger lickin' amazing! I tweaked the recipe a bit according to some other reviews. I cut two large sweet potatoes into chunks and added small red baby potatoes to the pan. When there was 20 minutes left on the timer, I added carrot chips to the pan. Then I broiled the meat on high for about 5 minutes to get extra crisp and darkness on the leg quarters. There was a greal deal of flavor, and each member of my family only had ONE serving, as it was so hearty.

Really good, but quite greasy with all that butter. I used honey instead of syrup and it came out really tasty. I also had trouble getting everything browned so had to stick it under the broiler for a few minutes at the end. It worked well and the end result was delicious
Use boneless chicken and skinless makes less flavor but still great
Was a great hit at my home!! Potatoes were awesome!!
This is a family favourite on regular rotation

My first time trying this recipe was easy to prepare, put carrots potatoes and I added some brussel sprouts with the Chicken Leg Quarters so fingers crossed, going to coat my chicken just before I bring it out of the oven with some Jack Daniels BBQ Sauce.

One of my top 5!! So much flavor. Don’t know what some of these reviews are talking about. It’s not rocket science. If you like a lot of flavor then add garlic salt, Italian seasonings, onion powder etc. I added carrots and extra butter with extra seasonings.
Easy to make and awesome flavors. I'm addicted

Looked and tasted great. I added onions and carrots to the pan. I used less garlic and peeled it. I spiced up the dish with garlic powder and sazon spice. Vegetables were deliciously done and moist. You don't really taste the syrup but it browns everything ever so nicely.

I loved the potatoes!! The chicken was a bit dry but that might be because I put them on top of the potatoes as I didn’t have space. Make sure you use a lot of garlic the recipe said I put less thinking it will be to much and I wished I put more!! Delicious 🤤
This was an easy recipe and it was ok. It has a lot of cooking time for the overall end results. Again not terrible, but not great.
